outcomes.description: Replace the image background with a basketball court.

nodes.question: Does the edited image show the background changed into a basketball court?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the background itself is recognizably a basketball court, supported by visible court context such as a playing surface and court markings; basketball equipment may support this judgment but equipment alone is insufficient. Fail if the background is clearly not a basketball court. Unknown if the background cannot be assessed reliably.
nodes.binding: Judge whether the requested background replacement is complete: the background must read as a basketball court, not merely contain basketball-related objects.

nodes.question: Is there visible evidence that the background has begun changing toward a basketball court, even though the requested court background is not complete?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image shows a discernible but incomplete change of the background toward a basketball court. Fail if there is no visible progress toward that change. Unknown if progress cannot be distinguished from the original or assessed reliably.
nodes.binding: Assess progress only toward replacing the background with a basketball court; unrelated edits do not count.

nodes.question: Replace the image background with a basketball court.
nodes.criteria: Return complete if s1 passes. Otherwise, return absent only if s1 fails and s2 fails, establishing no requested progress. Return partial if s1 fails and s2 passes, establishing incomplete progress toward the court background. Return unknown if the evidence needed to distinguish these outcomes is unresolved. A pass on s2 does not establish completion, and unrelated edits do not count.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. You receive no reference label or optimization feedback. Return status, evidence, reported confidence (0..1 or null), and used_dependency_ids naming every supplied context check_id exactly once in saved order.
Supports receive source and edited images. Answer only the saved proposition using its binding and criteria. Use pass/fail/unknown. Context is advisory unless listed in required_dependencies. A negative context observation is usable evidence. Unknown, skipped, or invalid context is not a failure and must not stop an independent image inspection. Inspect the images yourself; do not repeat a parent's answer. Return unknown when the relevant fact cannot be established. Confidence reports confidence in this answer, not calibrated correctness.
Fulfillment receives NO images. Use only saved support evidence, original instruction/rubric and frozen composition criteria. Return complete/partial/absent/unknown. Supporting passes answer specific propositions, not a count of completed edits. Their polarity can differ. Apply saved alternatives: optional uncertainty need not prevent a known outcome, but a required unresolved fact makes that outcome unresolved. Never invent a visual fact or convert missing evidence into failure. A conditional skip is not non-applicability. All applicable requested outcomes complete gives yes; no requested progress gives no; known progress short of completion gives partial. Unrelated changes are not progress.

fulfillment: The binding is underspecified: “Target: The background (...) a basketball court” does not clearly distinguish a complete court background from basketball-themed props or partial progress. Make the completion criterion explicitly assess the background as a whole, using recognizable playing surface and court markings as evidence; treat hoops or balls alone as progress, not completion. Preserve the existing s1/s2 decision logic and required checks, but clarify their distinct roles so s2 passing cannot be mistaken for completion and conflicting evidence yields unknown. In the supplied edit, the kitchen is replaced and a hoop, balls, and a court-like floor/line are visible, while much of the surrounding background is plain dark; this supports progress, but whether the court is recognizable enough for completion is the key criterion ambiguity. The reference label is aggregate guidance, not proof that any single feature is mandatory. All traces are valid and queried, so this is not a transport or dependency failure; high confidence and repeated partial labels do not resolve the visual threshold. Tighten the binding to require evidence-based whole-scene judgment and calibrated uncertainty at that threshold, without forcing the reference answer or adding unsupported constraints.
s2: The node’s wording asks only whether the background has begun changing, so it can pass on basketball props or partial court cues without resolving whether the requested background change is complete. Clarify the binding and criteria to distinguish discernible progress from completion, and keep this support check’s progress judgment separate from the completion check; a complete court should not fail merely because it is no longer incomplete. Judge the background as a whole: the edited image replaces the kitchen with a dark court-like setting and shows a hoop, balls, and floor markings, but the extent to which it reads as a complete basketball-court background is the relevant threshold—not any single feature. Preserve the existing checks and route genuinely ambiguous evidence to unknown rather than forcing a label. All traces are valid and queried, so this is a semantic criterion/routing issue, not a transport or dependency failure. Repeated high-confidence partial judgments and the aggregate reference label are investigation signals, not atomic ground truth.
s1: The node’s binding is already framed as a completion judgment, but the traces expose a threshold ambiguity: the edited image clearly replaces the kitchen with a basketball-themed scene and shows a hoop, balls, and a light floor with a curved line, while much of the background is dark and lacks clearly legible court context. Refine the typed criterion to judge whether the background as a whole is recognizable as a basketball court, weighing the visible floor and markings in context rather than treating any single feature as mandatory; distinguish partial basketball-themed progress from completion and use unknown when the visual evidence genuinely cannot settle that distinction. Keep this completion check separate from any progress check, and do not let a progress result substitute for completion. All traces are valid, queried, and dependency-free, so this is not a transport or schema failure. Repeated high-confidence failures and the aggregate reference label are signals to inspect the criterion and calibration, not atomic ground truth; do not force a yes or add unsupported requirements.

actions.question: Beyond basketball equipment and a limited strip of marked floor, does the visible background establish a basketball-court setting?
actions.criteria: Pass if the visible background as a whole is recognizably a basketball court, with enough court surface or surrounding court context to establish the requested background replacement. Fail if the court identity is conveyed only by isolated basketball equipment or a small amount of court surface while the remaining background is not recognizably a court. Unknown if the visible background does not permit a reliable judgment.
actions.binding: Assess whether the edited background fulfills the request to change the background into a basketball court. Use the source image only as context for the requested replacement; do not infer completion from basketball props alone.

actions.criteria: Return complete only if s1 passes and s1a passes, establishing both recognizable court features and a sufficiently established court background. If completion is not established, return partial when s2 passes, since it indicates requested progress; return absent only when s2 fails and the evidence establishes no requested progress. Return unknown when the evidence needed to distinguish these outcomes is unresolved. A pass on s1 alone does not establish completion, and unrelated edits do not count.

semantic_rejection.reason: The chain makes s1, s1a, and s2 all required for fulfillment, so an unknown or skipped progress check can block a complete result even when s1 and s1a establish completion. It also makes s1a a required completion condition, although the original rubric requires only that the requested change be complete; the extra whole-background test can reject a visibly completed court background based on an unsupported interpretation.
semantic_rejection.source_clause: yes means all requested changes are complete
semantic_rejection.counterexample: The edited image visibly has a basketball-court background with recognizable court features, so the requested change is complete, but s1a fails because the background is judged not to read as a coherent court setting, or s2 is unknown/skipped. Fulfillment cannot return complete because all three checks are required, despite the original rubric's completion criterion being met.
